summary: Carter County tower completed in 1946; about 70 ft steel tower now reached through MDC's Peck Ranch Conservation Area by a hike from a parking lot; climbing rules not stated.

facts.agency: Missouri Department of Conservation (tower access is through Peck Ranch Conservation Area)

access.note: Reached through Peck Ranch Conservation Area. MDC describes a gravel road to a parking lot, then a hike up the tower road. No source read says whether the tower may be climbed.

visit.trail_note: MDC: from the parking lot you can hike up the tower road to the fire tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1947-48 state manual places the tower in Deer Run State Forest; MDC's current page places the access road in Peck Ranch Conservation Area. The sources do not explain the change, so we report both.

notes_for_editor: The record id spells the name 'stegrall'; both sources spell it Stegall Mountain, so the id is left as is. The 1962 event comes from a source that reads 'FY 1962-03', apparently a typo for the 1962-64 biennium; the report's own title reads 7/1962 to 6/1964. The 70 ft figure is an 'about' from the 1963 survey. Search snippets (not fetched) claim a 100 ft height and an Aermotor MC-39 design; not cited. Hiking-site snippets suggest the tower is still reached on foot; the MDC page is the cited source. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story now says the tower 'appears to still stand' from the MDC page's hike description, and the 'no lookout named' point is limited to the reports read.
